sources.metric: Gujarat RTI Rules 2010: fee, payment modes, copy/inspection charges, BPL exemption, appeal forms, citizenship check
sources.source_name: Gujarat Right to Information Rules, 2010 (GAD notification GS/2112010/VHS/1005/2664/RTI Cell, Gazette Extra No. 40, 22-03-2010), copy hosted by SMC
sources.access_notes: This is an OCR'd scan: the text can be extracted but has OCR noise. Rule 3(1): apply on Form A, on plain paper with the same details, or by e-media. An e-media applicant must pay the fee within 7 days or the application is treated as withdrawn. Rule 3(2): the Rs 20 application fee can be paid in cash where a receipt facility exists, or by DD, pay order, non-judicial stamp or stamp paper, franking, e-stamping, court fee stamp, judicial stamp paper, IPO, revenue stamp, or treasury challan (head 0070-60-800-(17)). Rule 3(4): other charges can only be paid by cash, DD, pay order, IPO or challan, not by stamps. Rule 5: copies are Rs 2 per page for A4/A3 and actual cost for larger paper; inspection is free for the first half hour, then Rs 20 per half hour; samples at actual cost; floppy/CD Rs 50. BPL applicants are exempt from both the application fee and other charges if they attach a certified or true copy of the BPL card or certificate. Rule 4: transfer on Form D within 5 days. Rule 6: first appeal on Form E within 30 days; second appeal to GIC within 90 days, with the details listed in the rule. Rule 7: the PIO may verify citizenship, within the s.7 time limit. There is no word limit and no one-subject rule. Gujarati version: .../Gujarat_RTI_rules_2010_Guj.pdf.
sources.granularity: state (applies to all state PAs including SMC, AMC and Collectorates)
sources.latest_period: 2010 rules; no later amendment to fee rules found

sources.metric: GIC FAQ: application language, fee modes, BPL proof rules, online second appeal
sources.source_name: Gujarat Information Commission FAQs
sources.access_notes: Applications can be in English, Hindi or the official language of the area (Gujarati). They can be submitted in person, by post, or electronically where an online facility exists. The fee is Rs 20 under the 2010 Rules. It cites GAD circular PRCH-102018-1527-RTI Cell dated 05-12-2018: a BPL ration card does NOT qualify for fee exemption; the applicant needs a BPL card or a competent-authority certificate. Second appeals can be filed online via eApplication.aspx. The same FAQ covers the documents needed for a second appeal.

sources.metric: State executive instructions on RTI practice (free pages, e-delivery, inspection photos)
sources.source_name: GAD circular GAD/MRT/e-file/1/2023/1655/RTI Cell (approved 06-05-2025), acting on GIC Annual Report 2023-24 recommendations
sources.access_notes: The Unicode Gujarati text has broken conjuncts after extraction. Key points: (i) up to 5 pages of information are to be given free; (ii) for requests made by email or the online portal, send scans or photos after the copy fee is paid, with no physical copy; (iii) allow photography during inspection, and (iv) allow pen drives; FAAs must pass speaking orders; the s.4(1)(b) PAD must be updated every year. The GIC home page links to this circular.

sources.metric: Online RTI filing for Gujarat state PAs (including municipal corporations)
sources.source_name: Gujarat Online RTI Portal (ARTD/GAD + GIL/DST)
sources.access_notes: Live in Sep 2026, with a maintenance notice for 10-11 Aug 2026. The banner says 'RTI Application is in phased-wise roll-out'. Registration is mandatory. Payment options: SBI net banking, debit/credit card, wallets. BPL applicants upload a certificate. First appeal is filed online with no fee. There is no public list of onboarded PAs. The FAQ looks copied from the central portal: it wrongly says second appeals go to the CIC and has a 'XXXX characters' placeholder for the length limit. Help line 079-23258077. sources.metric: Why GIC rejects second appeals (walkthrough error-proofing)
sources.source_name: GIC analysis of rejected appeals/complaints, Jul-Dec 2024
sources.access_notes: 337 rejections. Causes: more than one second appeal filed (105); one appeal covering more than one Form A (74); no first appeal filed (55); more than 90 days after the FAA order (26); central PA (21); more than 135 days after the first appeal (20); complaint covering more than one Form A (18); second appeal before 45 days from the first appeal (6); missing documents (5); not a PA (5); complaint more than 30 days after cause with no condonation request (2). Encode these as validation rules.

scores.rationale: Surat is clearly easier to support in the RTI dimension. SMC runs the best municipal RTI disclosure found in Gujarat: a PIO/AA directory updated in Dec 2025, twenty years of annual returns in parseable English (up to FY2025-26), a quarterly return with within-time disposal and pendency, published first-appeal and GIC orders, PADs refreshed in May-Jun 2026, its own status tracker, and a link to the state online portal. That is enough to fill the RTI Tracker for the city corporation with official, citable numbers. It loses points because the PIO list and Patrak-7 use legacy Gujarati fonts, the Collectorate PADs are scanned, and appeal orders need OCR. AMC's RTI section has barely changed since 2011: PIO list from 2011, statistics only to 2010-11, superseded 2005 rules, 2022-24 PADs, and a site that breaks standard TLS clients. So both AMC RTI statistics and a current PIO directory would have to come from RTI requests, which is useful as the project's first demo template but slow. Ahmedabad scores back some points for the better Collectorate contact list, explicit filing at civic centres, MAGP's presence and nearness to GIC. The state layer (Rules 2010, GIC ticker, annual report, decisions DB, SNS benchmarks) is shared, so it does not favour either city.

challenges: City vs district mismatch: upstream RTI modules are district-scoped, but SMC and AMC are separate public authorities from the Surat and Ahmedabad Collectorates, Police Commissionerates, SUDA/AUDA and district courts. The RTI Tracker needs a per-PA key (PA name + administrative department), not just districtId.

The AMC website fails with OpenSSL 3 (unsafe legacy renegotiation, error 0A000152) and has an incomplete certificate chain. Scrapers need a custom OPENSSL_CONF with UnsafeLegacyRenegotiation and a CA bundle fix. WebFetch-style tools and Vercel/Node default fetch will fail.

Legacy ASCII-mapped Gujarati fonts (Terafont/LMG-style) appear in the SMC PIO list, SMC Patrak-7, the AMC 2011 PIO list and the Surat Collectorate PADs. The text layer is mojibake and needs a legacy-to-Unicode converter. Numbers, phones and emails survive. Unicode PDFs (GIC report in KrishnaUni, AMC PAD in Shruti, Ahmedabad Collectorate lists) have broken conjuncts after extraction.
Scanned PDFs need OCR with Gujarati support (e.g. tesseract guj): GIC orders hosted by SMC, Surat Collectorate PAD pages, the AMC Gujarati Form A and one AMC rules PDF.

Per-PA RTI statistics live in the login-only rti-ar.gujarat.gov.in. GIC reports only by department and says about 24% of applications are uploaded after its report, so statewide numbers are revised later. Store 'as-published' and 'revised' values.
SMC Patrak-7 is overwritten each quarter at a fixed URL, so each quarter must be archived on scrape to build a time series.

GIC decisions search is an ASP.NET postback with viewstate. It took more than 150 s for one month, is paginated, and exposes applicant names. The GIC daily board (CauseList.aspx) returned HTTP 500 on 27-09-2026.

The Gujarat online RTI portal is in phased rollout with no public list of onboarded PAs. Its FAQ is partly copied from the central portal: it wrongly says second appeals go to the CIC and has an 'XXXX characters' limit. News reports defects: unclear reply dates, a forced 'delay reason' on first appeals, and missing PIO names. The app can link to it but cannot deep-link a specific PA.

Upstream code will not work for Gujarat as-is. scrapeRTI hard-codes kic.karnataka.gov.in for every district and would write Karnataka rows under Gujarat districtIds. Its Prisma writes are not awaited (300 ms sleep hack). There is no Gujarat StateConfig, so getModuleSources falls back to a generic 'State Information Commission'. The File RTI button links only to rtionline.gov.in, which is wrong for SMC, AMC and Collectorates. The local-language heading is hard-coded to Kannada. pendingPct divides by filed+pending, and the value is mislabelled.

The RtiTemplate schema lacks the fields a Gujarat walkthrough needs: PA type (state, central or court), payment modes, FAA name and address, second-appeal body, deadline logic, and the language of the template. It also needs Gujarati templateTextLocal rendering.

Legal/product cautions: (1) RTI is for Indian citizens only. Gujarat Form A carries a citizenship declaration, and Rule 7 lets the PIO verify it. (2) A postal address is required. (3) Ask for records ('certified copies of...', 'number of...', 'list of...'), not opinions or 'why' questions, which PIOs can reject as not 'information' under s.2(f). (4) Section 8/9/11 exemptions exist, and the DPDP-amended s.8(1)(j) now bars personal information more broadly (SMC already cited it 14 times in 2025-26). (5) The app should not give legal advice; add a disclaimer and refer users to the MAGP helpline. (6) Storing applicant names and addresses makes the project a Data Fiduciary under DPDP 2023, with main duties phased in by about May 2027. Minimise data, prefer client-side generation, and get explicit consent. (7) GIC has capped 'disproportionate' applicants (a Surat family at 6 per year), so discourage bulk or omnibus filings.

Walkthrough rules to encode from GIC rejection data: one second appeal per RTI application; a first appeal must come first; a second appeal only after the FAA order or after 45 days without one, within 90 days of the order (GIC rejects appeals filed more than 135 days after the first appeal); a complaint within 30 days of the cause or with a condonation request; no central PAs at GIC; the BPL ration card is not valid proof; e-media applicants must pay within 7 days; district courts charge Rs 50 (Rs 500 for tender information); central PAs charge Rs 10 via rtionline.gov.in.

The GIC website (Sep 2026) shows the State Chief Information Commissioner post as vacant, with 5 SICs sitting. That may affect second-appeal timelines; the GIC ticker shows pendency rising in Aug 2026 (624 at opening, 1,039 at closing).

**Timelines and appeals** (RTI Act, plus the Gujarat Rules 2010 where they add something):
- **Reply:** within 30 days, or 48 hours where life or liberty is involved. Add 5 days if the application went through an APIO. Where a third party is involved under s.11, the limit is 40 days.
- **Deemed refusal:** no reply in time counts as a refusal under s.7(2).
- **Transfer:** a PIO must transfer an application to the right PA within 5 days under s.6(3), using Form D.
- **Late replies:** if the PIO misses the deadline, the information must be given free under s.7(6).
- **First appeal:** to the FAA on Form E within 30 days. The FAA should decide in 30 days, or 45 at most.
- **Second appeal or complaint:** to GIC within 90 days, on the GIC form or online.
- **Language:** English, Hindi or Gujarati.
- **Fee:** Rs 20, with no word limit and no one-subject rule.
- **Free pages:** under the GAD circular of May 2025, up to 5 pages are free.

**What the upstream RTI module does:**
- **RTI Tracker (/rti):** reads RtiStat rows (department, year, month, filed, disposed, pending, avgDays, source). It shows headline cards, a pendency bar, a department-wise stacked bar chart and a full table, with an AI insight card and a data-source banner. When there are no rows it shows an empty state.
- **File RTI (/file-rti):** a 'wizard' that is really a picker. It lists that district's RtiTemplate rows, shows the PIO address, fee, template text, local-language text and a tip, and offers copy-to-clipboard and a 'File Online' link to rtionline.gov.in.
- **Scraper:** scheduled daily at 2 AM for every active district, but it only works for Karnataka.
- **Templates:** added through per-city seed scripts (for example prisma/seed-pune-rti.ts). A Gujarat port needs a new StateConfig with GIC, the onlinerti.gujarat.gov.in portal URL and Gujarati text.

**Recommended data plan for Surat:**
- Parse the SMC annual-return PDFs for 2005-2026 into RtiStat at PA level: filed, disposed and pending, plus rejections by section and fees in extra columns.
- Archive Patrak-7 every quarter to get within-time disposal and pendency.
- Scrape the GIC ticker monthly as a state-level context card.
- Load the SNS report-card figures once a year.

**For Ahmedabad:** file the AMC annual-statistics and PIO-directory RTIs first. They double as the project's first live demonstration.
